Day 55 of 100 · Networking Deep Dive

DHCP

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityNetworking Deep DivePublished artifact recovered

DHCP automatically leases clients network configuration through the Discover, Offer, Request and Acknowledge exchange.

Architecture / mental model

client UDP 68 ⇄ server UDP 67 · Discover → Offer → Request → ACK

How it works

A new DHCPv4 client begins without enough configuration for ordinary unicast networking, so discovery commonly relies on broadcast behavior to locate available servers.

The DORA sequence negotiates an offered address and associated options such as subnet mask/prefix, default gateway, DNS servers and lease duration.

A lease is temporary configuration with a lifecycle. Clients renew rather than treating an assigned address as permanent identity.

Hands-on reference

ip addr
ip route
resolvectl status
sudo tcpdump -ni any 'port 67 or port 68'

Verification

Capture a DHCP lease acquisition in a lab and identify client/server direction for Discover, Offer, Request and ACK.

Field note / gotcha

The port direction is easy to reverse: DHCP servers use UDP 67 and clients use UDP 68.

Security considerations

Untrusted DHCP servers can provide malicious gateway or DNS configuration. Network access controls such as DHCP snooping may be appropriate on managed switching infrastructure.

What I learned

Automatic addressing is a protocol conversation, not a magical property of connecting a cable.
